_note: Klingon interface. Written in English, unlike the Hungarian and Greek notes and like the Indonesian one, and for a reason rather than out of laziness: this note is documentation for whoever reviews the catalogue, and two thousand words of Klingon prose would be a far larger act of composition than the 318 strings it describes. SOURCE: every string is built from headwords in the published Klingon lexicon (TKD, its addendum, KGT, Talk Now! Klingon, and the qep'a' and qepHom'a' new-word releases) with the morphology TKD sections 3 and 4 documents. **No root here is an invention**, which is the same rule the corpus follows, and it is checkable the same way: strip a pronominal prefix and any suffixes and the remainder is a dictionary entry. REGISTER: the imperative, everywhere an English interface would use a bare verb. `yIpol` "save it", `yIngeH` "send it", `yIwIv` "choose it". Klingon has no T-V distinction and no politeness register in the European sense, so an imperative on a button is not brusque -- it is the only thing the grammar offers, and KGT's own examples of everyday instruction are imperatives (`Soj yIDIl!`, `DaH yIDIl!`). The prefix is `yI-` where the object is a thing and `HI-` where it is the reader (`HIboQ` "assist me", which is the studio's *Help me decide*), and `tI-` for a plural object (`Dochmey tIchel`). TERMS: `nav` is a sheet of paper and `tenwal` a page or printed face -- Klingon already keeps those apart, so no word had to be stretched. `war` is a column in a table and `wev` a row, both from the lexicon's own spreadsheet vocabulary, which is exactly the distinction `format.columnsPerFace` and `format.columnsShown` need and which English collapses into one word. Also: `'echletHom` = card, `ngutlh` = letter or glyph, `ngutlh Segh` = typeface, `ngutlh 'ab` = type size, `qalmuS` = colour, `rItlh` = ink, `veH` = margin (literally boundary), `rulvaH` = gap, `chevwI'` = divider, `yamtaw` = the printed rule, `botlh` = middle, `'utlh` = the header band, `potlh` = importance, `'ay'` = section, `De'` = data or content, `lol` = attitude or arrangement, used for the format panel. `'uj` renders the inch: it is a Klingon unit of 34.83 cm and not an inch at all, so the number beside it is right and the unit is a borrowing -- flagged here because it is the one term in the catalogue that is knowingly imprecise. Serif and Sans stay Latin, as they do in the Greek and Indonesian catalogues, and the romanisation-system names stay as printed, being standards initialisms. INTERPOLATION -- and Klingon comes out of this better than any other language here, for a reason worth stating. A placeholder is a plain string substitution, so the danger everywhere else is a template that needs its insert to inflect. **Klingon's noun suffixes have no allomorphs**: there is one locative `-Daq`, one ablative `-vo'`, one benefactive `-vaD`, and they attach to any noun unchanged. So `{language}Daq` is safe in a way `{language}ban/-ben` is not in Hungarian and `el {language}` is not in Spanish, and Klingon has no articles at all, so the article trap cannot arise either. Two traps do arise and both are avoided here. (1) **The type-4 possessives and the type-2 plurals are chosen by the noun's class, not by its sound**: `-wI'`/`-wIj` for "my" and `-pu'`/`-Du'`/`-mey` for the plural split on whether the noun is capable of using language, or is a body part, or is neither. That is a property of the *inserted* word, which a substitution cannot see, so no template in this file puts a possessive or a plural suffix after a placeholder. Where the English says "{language} pocket guide" the Klingon says `{language} 'echletHom`, two bare nouns in a noun-noun compound, which needs no suffix at all. (2) **Capitalisation is phonemic**: `q` and `Q` are different consonants and `I` is a vowel while `i` is not a letter. So no template may uppercase or lowercase a placeholder, and none does. This is also why the respelling table for a Klingon reader cannot use the `caps` stress device -- see data/respell/rules/tlh__tlh-TA.json. WORD ORDER: Klingon is object-verb-subject and puts a time element first, so a template with a placeholder in the middle of a clause has to be written so the insert is a whole noun phrase in its own slot. `{target} → {source}` and `{language} Hol` are the two shapes used; nothing here asks a placeholder to sit inside a verb. WHAT IS NOT HERE: `format.reserve.ios` and `.android` are `'ayvon` and `'anDroy'`, which are transliterations of brand names rather than lexicon entries, and are the only two coinages in the catalogue. They are marked here rather than left to be discovered. Klingon has no attested word for a tax refund, so `quiz.interest.business.hint` carries the English `tax`.
